Using the approximation $ \log(2^n) = n \log 2 $, we can estimate the probability that **none** of the 2002 numbers is prime: $$
\left(1 - \frac{1}{n \log 2}\right)^{2002} \approx \exp\left( - \frac{2002}{n \log 2} \right)
$$

So the **expected number of $ n \geq 2001 $** for which **none** of the $ k_i 2^n + 1 $ is prime is: $$
\sum_{n=2001}^{\infty} \exp\left( - \frac{2002}{n \log 2} \right)
$$

sentence: This sum **diverges**, because the exponential decay is too slow.
